results.title: Kourovka Problem 18.15: an inner twisted class that is not a subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Every nontrivial group $G$ with trivial centre has an element $a \in G$ such that, for the inner automorphism $\varphi(g) = aga^{-1}$, the twisted conjugacy class of the identity $[e]_\varphi = \{g^{-1}\varphi(g) : g \in G\}$ is not a subgroup of $G$.

results.title: Negative answer to Kourovka Problem 18.15
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The conjecture of Kourovka Problem 18.15 is false: there is a nontrivial group $G$ with trivial centre such that for every $a \in G$, with $\varphi$ the inner automorphism $\varphi(g) = aga^{-1}$, the twisted conjugacy class of the identity $[e]_\varphi = \{g^{-1}\varphi(g) : g \in G\}$ is a subgroup of $G$.

results.title: Killing fields on Euclidean space
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space, viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given by its inner product. A vector field $V$ on $F$ is Killing if and only if $V$ is $C^\infty$ and its derivative is skew-adjoint at every point: for all $x, u, w \in F$, $\langle DV(x)\,u, w \rangle + \langle u, DV(x)\,w \rangle = 0$.

results.title: Translations are Killing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space, viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given by its inner product. For every $c \in F$, the constant vector field $y \mapsto c$ on $F$ is Killing.

results.title: Linear Killing fields on Euclidean space
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space, viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given by its inner product, and let $A \colon F \to F$ be a continuous linear map. The linear vector field $y \mapsto A y$ is Killing if and only if $A$ is skew-adjoint: $\langle A u, w \rangle + \langle u, A w \rangle = 0$ for all $u, w \in F$.

results.title: Padovan-like sequence for Schreier sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $q$, the sequence $a_{p,q,n}$, $n \ge 0$, is defined as follows. If $q \ge 1$ and $n \ge p + q$, then $a_{p,q,n} = a_{p,q,n-q} + a_{p,q,n-p-q}$. results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $\ell$, $k$ and $q$, $|E_{n,\ell,k,q}|$ is the number of partitions of $n$ into exactly $k$ parts, all at least $\ell$, whose largest part exceeds the second largest part (counted with multiplicity) by exactly $q$; such a partition has at least two parts, so the count is $0$ for $k < 2$.

results.title: Partitions avoiding parts from 2 up to a bound
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Partitions avoiding parts from 2 up to a bound and large even parts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $\ell$, $|H_{n,\ell}|$ is the number of partitions of $n$ none of whose parts lies in $\{2, \dots, \ell\}$ and none of whose parts is an even number greater than $2\ell$.

results.title: Compositions with exactly $s$ parts, each at least $v$

results.title: First non-multiples of an integer
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $u$ and $n$, $G_{u,n}$ is the set of positive integers $k \le un$ with $u \nmid k$ such that at most $n$ of the integers in $[1, k]$ are not divisible by $u$. results.title: Schreier sets avoiding multiples
results.caption: Definition

Then $|D_{u,n}|$ is the number of Schreier sets $F \subseteq G_{u,n}$ with $\lfloor (un - 1)/(u - 1) \rfloor \in F$.

results.title: Weighted Schreier-type sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, let $\omega_k(E)$ denote the number of elements of a finite set $E$ that are different from $k$. The weighted Schreier count $a_{k,n}$ is the number of subsets $E \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ that are empty or satisfy $\omega_k(E) < \min E$.

results.title: Seeded partial sums
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, and let $s = (s_n)_{n \ge 0}$ (the seed sequence) and $a = (a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be sequences in $M$. The seeded partial sums $t^s_{k,n}$, for $k, n \ge 0$, are defined by recursion on $k$: $t^s_{0,n} = a_n$ and $t^s_{k+1,n} = s_k + \sum_{i\lt n} t^s_{k,i}$.

results.title: Iterated partial sums
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and let $a = (a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence in $M$. For $k, m \ge 0$, the $k$-fold iterated partial sum $P^{(k)}(a)(m)$ is the seeded partial sum $t^s_{k,m}$ of $a$ for the zero seed sequence $s = 0$. Thus $P^{(0)}(a)(m) = a_m$ and $P^{(k+1)}(a)(m) = \sum_{i\lt m} P^{(k)}(a)(i)$.

results.title: Seeded partial sums start at the seed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, let $s = (s_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $a = (a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be sequences in $M$, and write $t^s_{k,n}$ for the seeded partial sums of $a$ with seed sequence $s$. Then $t^s_{k+1,0} = s_k$ for every $k \ge 0$.

results.title: The first iterated partial sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and let $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence in $M$. For every $m \ge 0$, the $1$-fold iterated partial sum of $(a_n)$ at $m$ is the ordinary partial sum: $P^{(1)}((a_n)_{n \ge 0})(m) = \sum_{i\lt m} a_i$.

results.title: Recurrence for iterated partial sums
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, let $a = (a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence in $M$, and write $P^{(k)}(a)(m)$ for its $k$-fold iterated partial sum at $m$. Then for all $k, m \ge 0$, $P^{(k+1)}(a)(m+1) = P^{(k+1)}(a)(m) + P^{(k)}(a)(m)$.

results.title: Diagonal weighted Schreier counts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$, the weighted Schreier count satisfies $a_{n,n} = 2F_n$, where $F_n$ is the $n$-th Fibonacci number ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$).

results.title: Weighted Schreier counts for $k = 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $\ell$, the weighted Schreier count satisfies $a_{1,1+\ell} = F_{\ell+2} + 1$, where $F_j$ is the $j$-th Fibonacci number ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$).

results.title: Weighted Schreier counts on and above the diagonal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a_{k,n}$ be the weighted Schreier count and let $F_n$ denote the Fibonacci numbers, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. For all $k \ge 2$ and $\ell \ge 0$, $a_{k,k+\ell} = 2\sum_{i=0}^{k-2} \binom{\ell}{i} F_{k-i} + 2\binom{\ell}{k-1} + \sum_{j=1}^{\ell} \binom{j}{\ell-j+k}$.

results.title: Weighted Schreier counts for $0 < m < k$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $k \ge 2$ and $m$ with $0 < m < k$, the weighted Schreier count satisfies $a_{k,m} = F_{m+1}$, where $F_j$ is the $j$-th Fibonacci number ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$).

results.title: Weighted Schreier counts equal twice a Fibonacci number for small offsets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a_{k,n}$ be the weighted Schreier count and let $F_n$ denote the Fibonacci numbers, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. For all $k, \ell \ge 0$ with $k \ge \ell + 2$, we have $a_{k,k+\ell} = 2F_{k+\ell}$.

results.title: Recurrence for weighted Schreier counts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$ with $k \ge 1$, $n > k$ and $n > 2$, the weighted Schreier counts satisfy $a_{k,n} = a_{k,n-1} + a_{k-1,n-2}$. At $k = 1$ the term $a_{0,n-2}$ is the same count with $\omega_0(E)$, the number of elements of $E$ different from $0$, equal to the number $|E|$ of all elements of $E$, since no element of a set $E \subseteq \{1, \dots, n-2\}$ equals $0$.

results.title: Effect of the seed on seeded partial sums
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $a = (a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $b = (b_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be sequences in $R$, and write $t^b_{k,n}$ for the seeded partial sums of $a$ with seed sequence $b$ and $t^0_{k,n}$ for those with the zero seed sequence. Then for all $k, n \ge 0$, $t^b_{k,n} - t^0_{k,n} = \sum_{i\lt k} \binom{n}{i} b_{k-1-i}$, where the binomial coefficients are read as elements of $R$.

results.title: Adding one to a sequence shifts its iterated partial sums by a binomial coefficient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence in $R$, and let $k, m \ge 0$. Writing $P^{(k)}(x)(m)$ for the $k$-fold iterated partial sum of a sequence $x$ at $m$, we have $P^{(k)}((a_n + 1)_{n \ge 0})(m) - P^{(k)}((a_n)_{n \ge 0})(m) = \binom{m}{k}$, where $\binom{m}{k}$ is read as an element of $R$.

results.title: Iterated partial sums of shifted Fibonacci numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F_n$ denote the Fibonacci numbers, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$, and write $P^{(k)}(x)(m)$ for the $k$-fold iterated partial sum of a sequence $x$ of natural numbers at $m$. Then for all $k, \ell \ge 0$, $P^{(k)}((F_{n+2})_{n \ge 0})(\ell) = P^{(k)}((F_n)_{n \ge 0})(\ell) + P^{(k)}((F_n)_{n \ge 0})(\ell + 1)$.

results.title: Weighted Schreier counts for $n < k$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n < k$, the weighted Schreier count satisfies $a_{k,n} = F_{n+1}$, where $F_j$ is the $j$-th Fibonacci number ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$).

results.title: The FACILITY LOCATION decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: FACILITY LOCATION is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a facility location instance that is well-formed and feasible; bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.

results.title: FACILITY LOCATION is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: FACILITY LOCATION belongs to NP, and every decision problem $L$ in NP reduces to FACILITY LOCATION by a polynomial-time many-one reduction: there is a polynomial-time computable map $f$ on bitstrings such that, for every bitstring $x$, $L$ accepts $x$ exactly when FACILITY LOCATION accepts $f(x)$.

results.title: Star height of a regular expression
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The star height of an ordinary regular expression is the nesting depth of the Kleene star in it: the expressions for the empty language and the empty word and the single letters have star height $0$; a union $e_1 + e_2$ and a concatenation $e_1 e_2$ have the larger of the star heights of $e_1$ and $e_2$; and $e^*$ has star height one more than $e$.

results.title: Generalized regular expressions
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A generalized regular expression over an alphabet $\alpha$ is built from ordinary regular expressions over $\alpha$ by complement, union, concatenation and Kleene star: every ordinary regular expression over $\alpha$ is one, and if $e$, $e_1$, $e_2$ are generalized regular expressions, then so are the complement $\neg e$, the union $e_1 + e_2$, the concatenation $e_1 e_2$ and the star $e^*$.

results.title: Bounded generalized star height
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A language $L$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ has generalized star height at most $n$, for a natural number $n$, if some generalized regular expression over $\alpha$ whose generalized star height is at most $n$ denotes $L$.

results.title: Event that the open cluster of a site is infinite
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The event `{x ↔ ∞}` that the open cluster of `x` is infinite.

results.title: Disconnected sites in infinite clusters give two infinite clusters
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If `x` and `y` both lie in infinite clusters, either they are connected or there are at least two infinite clusters.

results.title: Joint percolation at most connectivity given no two infinite clusters
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: With at most one infinite cluster almost surely, `μ(x ↔ ∞, y ↔ ∞) ≤ μ(x ↔ y)`.

results.title: Two-point lower bound from FKG, invariance, uniqueness and percolation
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If `μ` satisfies the FKG inequality for the events `{x ↔ ∞}` (`hPA`), is translation invariant on them (`hTI`), has at most one infinite cluster almost surely (`huniq`), and percolates (`htheta`), then `μ(0 ↔ x) ≥ θ²` for every `x`.

results.title: Crossing probabilities converge to the percolation probability
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For any finite measure, the probability that the origin is connected to the complement of the box of radius `n - 1` tends to the percolation probability.

results.title: Box-boundary connection probability tends to percolation probability
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For any finite measure, the probability that the origin is connected to the boundary of the box of radius `n` inside the box tends to the percolation probability.

results.title: A connection to outside the box passes through the box boundary
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: A connection from the origin to a site outside the box passes through the box boundary.

results.title: Uniform decay of two-point connectivity without percolation
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Without percolation, the two-point connectivity from the origin tends to zero uniformly: for every `ε > 0` there is `n` with `μ(0 ↔ x) < ε` for all `x` outside the box of radius `n`.
